record.paper_title: Operations Research challenges in forestry: 33 open problems
record.original_question: When multiple forestry organizations collaborate on transportation, joint planning can reduce total cost, but the participants still need fair rules for allocating gains while keeping sensitive data such as customers, agreements, and orders private. The open question is how to model practical collaboration in transportation together with efficient and acceptable sharing principles for the resulting benefits and costs.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6 How can we model and propose efficient sharing principles for practical collaboration in transportation?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a finite set N = {1, 2, ..., n} of organizations (for instance, forestry companies), each of which has its own transportation demand consisting of a set of orders to be moved between supply and demand locations under capacity, time-window, fleet, and routing constraints. For every coalition S ⊆ N let c(S) denote the minimum total transportation cost obtainable when the members of S pool their orders and jointly plan vehicle routes and schedules; assume c(∅) = 0 and that c is subadditive, so that joint planning may reduce cost compared with stand-alone operation.

When the grand coalition N collaborates, the realized total benefit is v(N) = Σ_{i∈N} c({i}) − c(N) ≥ 0. Each participant must, however, keep certain information private (its customer identities, contractual agreements, and individual order details) and will only join a collaboration whose cost/benefit allocation it considers acceptable.

The problem is the following:

(a) Propose a mathematical model of practical collaborative transportation among the organizations in N that captures the joint routing/scheduling optimization producing c(S) under realistic operational constraints, while respecting the privacy of each participant's sensitive data.

(b) Within this model, design an allocation rule φ : 2^N → R^n assigning to every coalition S a vector (φ_i(S))_{i∈S} of cost shares (or, equivalently, benefit shares) such that the rule is
  (i) efficient: Σ_{i∈S} φ_i(S) = c(S);
  (ii) individually rational: φ_i(S) ≤ c({i}) for every i ∈ S;
  (iii) stable in a cooperative-game-theoretic sense (e.g. lies in the core of (N, c) whenever the core is nonempty, or otherwise satisfies an explicit acceptability criterion);
  (iv) computable using only information that respects each participant's privacy constraints; and
  (v) acceptable to the participants in practice.

Provide such a model and sharing principle, or prove that no rule can simultaneously satisfy the listed requirements.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a list of operations-research challenges in forestry. While there is an extensive literature on collaborative vehicle routing and cost-allocation methods (Shapley value, nucleolus, equal profit method, etc.), no canonical solution has been recognized that simultaneously addresses realistic transportation collaboration, privacy, efficiency, and acceptability. The problem remains open in this general form.
